summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of a right renal transplant, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia, was admitted for evaluation and treatment of right renal artery stenosis. He presented with progressive hypertension, and a renal artery duplex suggested stenosis. He was admitted for preoperative hydration and underwent a successful CO2-guided renal arteriogram and stent placement the following day. The procedure was uncomplicated, and his kidney function remained stable postoperatively. He was discharged home the next day in stable condition with instructions to continue immunosuppressive, antihypertensive, and antiplatelet therapies, and to follow up with renal and vascular clinics in two weeks.
